From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Flexible tranche & surge plan for Quantico Analytics renewal

Hi Olivia —

Following up from our renewal touchpoint last week. We ran the Q2 utilization report on your Dedicated fleet and sketched a flexible-commit proposal that should better match what you actually use while keeping unit economics predictable. Attached: utilization_report_q2.pdf (high-level), and an initial commit sketch (I'll send a workbook once we sync on numbers).

High level recommendation:
- Baseline commit: 50 GPUs (predictable baseline coverage)
- Surge/burst pool: 20 GPUs reserved for predictable spikes, with option to burst to +50 GPUs on short notice (60-minute notice target)
- Granular tranche: 3-month micro-commits for the first 9 months to de-risk adoption and align to observed traffic patterns

Key asks from your side:
1) Can you confirm the quarterly 95th percentile sustained vCPU/GPU hours we should plan to cover? (I pulled a conservative estimate in the attached PDF)
2) Who should I loop on procurement for a clean PO/contract path?
3) Any SLA/uptime constraints beyond standard SLA you want to include for the surge window?

If it helps, I can convert the sketch into a concrete pricing workbook (commit_plan_v2.xlsx) and route through DocuSign for signatures once we lock numbers.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk through.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Accounts, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Thanks Jordan — this looks promising. A few quick clarifications before we escalate to procurement: 

- The baseline 50 GPUs aligns roughly with our steady-state predictions, but we had an unexpected 48-hour spike in May that pushed sustained usage up ~35%. We need to make sure the surge pool covers similar events.
- Can the burst pool be metered differently (e.g., post-pay for ephemeral bursts vs committed pricing)?
- Who owns the onboarding work for a new tranche (networking/VPC peering + security reviews)?

I'll defer pricing and signature logistics to procurement (cc'd). For onboarding, loop Dev Patel from your infra team if we proceed; he handled our initial Dedicated setup and did a great job.

Olivia
Olivia Martin
Head of AI Platforms, Quantico Analytics

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick reply and context. Based on the Q2 usage and the May spike you mentioned, here's an updated, actionable proposal: 

Overview
- Baseline commit: 50 GPUs (12-month term)
- Micro-commits: three 3-month tranches (15 GPUs each) that can convert to baseline at each tranche boundary
- Burst pool: 20 GPUs reserved; ephemeral burst up to +50 GPUs available on demand (billed at burst rate)

Operational notes (Dev supplied):
- Onboarding per tranche: ~18-24 engineer-hours for VPC peering, routing, and security review; KV cache warm-up for first warm requests estimated 30–60 minutes for core models
- Autoscaler warm pool: recommended pre-warm of 10 GPUs for 30 minutes during historically peak windows to keep token latency within SLA

Pricing sketch (summary)- Baseline committed GPU-hour: $X.XX (discount applied for 12-mo)
- Micro-commit GPU-hour: baseline less 5% (short-term micro-commit incentive)
- Burst GPU-hour (metered): baseline + 35% premium (post-pay for ephemeral usage)

Next steps
1) I'll attach a pricing workbook and a DocuSign envelope for the baseline + first micro-commit (link below).
2) Procurement to confirm PO pathway and expected sign-off dates.
3) If accepted, we slot a 2-week onboarding window with Dev for the first tranche.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/track/EXAMPLE-DOC-12345
Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-quantico-commit-plan

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the workbook.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
